topics.topic: Neeyat Ka Phal (The Fruit of Intent)
topics.notes: An Indian folk tale (public domain, oral tradition): a lazy woodcutter and a fakir's three wishes, each used wrong before the last is used wise.

topics.topic: Woh Jo Bolta Nahi Tha (The Boy Who Never Spoke)
topics.notes: A village folk tale about a mute boy who understands animals, and the drought only he can end.
A lesser-told Akbar-Birbal tale (public domain) retold as one continuous story, not a quiz format.
A Panchatantra fable (public domain) expanded into a full narrated story with real stakes.
Four strangers in a night train compartment; by morning one of them is not who they said they were.

topics.topic: The Letter That Arrived Ten Years Late
topics.notes: A letter delayed a decade by the postal system reopens a disappearance everyone had stopped asking about.
A locked, empty flat, and a cat that has clearly been fed every day for a week -- the small mystery that unravels a bigger one.
A theatre's understudy keeps getting the lead role, every time the lead has a convenient accident.
A hill-road night bus, a landslide ahead, a passenger who knows exactly when it will happen.
A bank employee discovers the vault's timer has been reset by someone already inside the building.
A woman realises the three missed calls on her phone are from a number that was disconnected two years ago.
A hostage negotiator realises halfway through the call that the hostage-taker is his own brother.

topics.topic: Kuldhara: The Night a Village Vanished
topics.notes: The real, documented 19th-century overnight abandonment of Kuldhara village, Rajasthan -- what is recorded, what is legend.

topics.topic: The Great Calcutta Fire Brigade Strike of 1897
topics.notes: A little-known real labour dispute during colonial Calcutta's plague year, told as a street-level story.

topics.topic: The Man Who Sold the Taj Mahal
topics.notes: The real 1946 con artist Natwarlal, who 'sold' the Taj Mahal as scrap -- documented reports, not legend.

topics.topic: The Last Flight of INS Khukri (1971)
topics.notes: The real sinking of INS Khukri in the 1971 India-Pakistan war, built from survivor accounts and naval records.

topics.topic: Savitri and Yama: The Argument With Death
topics.notes: The Mahabharata's Savitri-Satyavan story (public domain text), retold as one continuous narrated story.

topics.topic: The Churning of the Ocean (Samudra Manthan)
topics.notes: The Puranic myth of devas and asuras churning the cosmic ocean for amrit, told in full.
The Greek myth of Icarus and Daedalus (public domain), told for a Hinglish audience with its own warmth.
A Norse myth (public domain, Prose Edda) about Loki's bet that costs him his lips -- almost.

topics.topic: The River That Had No Name
topics.notes: Two estranged brothers raft an unmapped Himalayan river to scatter their father's ashes where he asked.

topics.topic: The Last Lighthouse Keeper of the Andamans
topics.notes: A fictional story built on the real isolation and cyclones of Andaman lighthouse postings.

topics.topic: Six Days to Everest Base Camp
topics.notes: A first-time trekker, a sudden storm, and a porter's local knowledge that saves the group.
A young man inherits his late father's smuggling route and must use it once, honestly, to save his sister.

topics.topic: The Last Letter My Father Wrote
topics.notes: A son finds an unfinished, unsent letter his father wrote him twenty years ago and finally reads it.
An old woman keeps a chair facing the window for the son who never came back from the city; this is the day he does.
A mother's small daily sacrifice during a hard year, seen only years later by the child she protected.
A strict schoolteacher's last day, and the one student who understood what the strictness was for.
Two commuters who have never spoken start leaving notes for each other on the same train seat.
An arranged match, a secret first love, and the one conversation that changes everyone's mind the right way.
Two widowed parents meet at their kids' school and slowly, awkwardly, fall for each other again.
A city rooftop garden becomes the one place two overworked neighbours actually talk, season by season.
A son-in-law convinced his mother-in-law is spying on his marriage is, technically, correct -- just not how he thinks.

topics.topic: The WhatsApp Group That Ruined the Wedding
topics.notes: A family wedding-planning group chat spirals into chaos after one autocorrect disaster.
A building's one working lift becomes the site of a petty, escalating, very Indian neighbourly feud.
A man's diet, his wife's cooking, and his best friend's terrible influence collide at every family function.

topics.topic: The Gift of the Magi, Hinglish Edition
topics.notes: O. Henry's public-domain story (died 1910) of a poor couple's Christmas gifts, retold as an Indian festival story.
Munshi Premchand's public-domain Hindi classic about a boy, a fair and a pair of tongs for his grandmother.
Maupassant's public-domain 'The Necklace' (died 1893), retold with an Indian middle-class setting and its own twist.
Rabindranath Tagore's public-domain story (died 1941) of a Kabuli fruitseller and a little girl, told whole.

topics.topic: The Dak Bungalow on the Old Highway
topics.notes: A travelling salesman takes shelter in an abandoned colonial-era dak bungalow during a storm -- one quiet, occasional horror tale.
A family photo on the wall shows one more person in it every year -- a slow-dread story, not gore.
A younger sister finds letters her late elder sister wrote but never sent, addressed to her future self.
A real, documented 19th-century chess prodigy of Lucknow and the colonial-era tournament that nearly erased his name.
